strategy_definition.summary: Identifies protected market structure using Intermediate Term Highs (ITH) and Lows (ITL). Short-term highs hold until an opposing ITL is taken, triggering a larger pullback into a higher-timeframe premium array.

timeframes.notes: Highly fractal. The presenter demonstrates moving from Daily -> 1H -> 15m -> 1m, emphasizing that pullbacks seek premium arrays on the timeframe immediately above the current one.

glossary.STH: Short Term High - synonymous with a standard swing high.
glossary.STL: Short Term Low - synonymous with a standard swing low.
glossary.ITH: Intermediate Term High - a swing high that is flanked by lower swing highs to its immediate left and right.
glossary.ITL: Intermediate Term Low - a swing low that is flanked by higher swing lows to its immediate left and right.
glossary.Draw on liquidity: The immediate target level price is reaching for, often an opposing ITL or ITH.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_high
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing high that has a lower swing high to the left of it and a lower swing high to the right of it.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: A sequence of 3 swing_highs where the price of index 1 > price of index 0 AND price of index 1 > price of index 2.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_low
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing low that has a higher swing low to the left of it and a higher swing low to the right of it.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: A sequence of 3 swing_lows where the price of index 1 < price of index 0 AND price of index 1 < price of index 2.

custom_signals.name: short_term_high
custom_signals.plain_definition: A standard swing high that is not an intermediate term high.

sequence: Price moves away from a higher timeframe premium array, creating an Intermediate Term High (ITH).
As price trends toward the Draw on Liquidity (the opposing ITL), it creates Short Term Highs (STHs).
These STHs are protected and should not be violated as long as the ITL has not been reached.
Price reaches and sweeps the targeted Intermediate Term Low.
Once the ITL is swept, expect a larger retracement into a premium array located on the timeframe immediately above the current execution timeframe.
The ITH formed before the ITL sweep now becomes the new protected high.

invalidation.text: If a protected Intermediate Term High is violated before the target Draw on Liquidity (ITL) is reached, the structure is broken.

filters.text: For the retracement after an ITL is swept, look for multiple PD arrays overlapping (e.g., an FVG overlapping with a mitigation block).

entry_rule.text: Enter during the larger retracement that occurs immediately after an ITL is taken, targeting a higher timeframe premium array.
entry_rule.quote: After we take that intermediate term low... retracement into a premium array that is above the one minute time frame.

target_rule.text: Target the opposing Intermediate Term Low (for a bearish setup).
target_rule.quote: our draw on liquidity is this intermediate term low

stop_rule.text: Place stop loss above the protected Intermediate Term High.
stop_rule.quote: this intermediate term high should ideally not get violated at all

presenter_claims.claim: Following this exact step-by-step logic will get you as close to the 'Holy Grail' as possible.
This strategy can yield a 90% win rate (with the caveat that 1 in 10 days will still be bad).

strategy_definition.notes: The strategy acts as a structural overlay for existing concepts (FVGs, Mitigation Blocks). It re-contextualizes standard swing highs into a hierarchy (STH vs ITH) to predict which highs are 'safe' for stop placement and when a trend will pause for a deep pullback.

confidence.reason: The presenter is extremely explicit about the definitions of ITH/ITL, the sequence of events, and which highs are protected versus targeted.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps an intermediate term high (which was a previous day high) and rejects heavily, creating a Daily bearish FVG.
Price moves out of the Daily premium array and targets a 1H discount array (an intermediate term low). It creates a series of protected short-term highs along the way.
Zooming in, the price action clearly shows intermediate term highs protecting the downward structure while sweeping intermediate term lows.
After sweeping a local 1m intermediate term low, price pulls back deeply into an overlapping 5m FVG and Mitigation Block. This retracement forms a new protected 1m intermediate term high.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter uses this continuous top-down sequence to illustrate the fractal nature of market structure. He emphasizes that predicting deeper retracements becomes highly probable once a Draw on Liquidity (an Intermediate Term Low) is swept, at which point traders should look one timeframe higher for the target premium array.

may_differ.reason: Traidle relies on a standard 3-candle swing point rule. The presenter's ITH/ITL concepts require sequences of multiple swings (a 3-swing fractal), which standard indicator engines do not inherently flag without compound logic.

uncertainties.why: Without seeing the video frames, exact asset symbols, times, prices, and candlestick OHLCV data cannot be identified. All frames have been submitted with empty candle arrays.
